problem:
Consider the function $f(x)={x}^{3}-6{x}^{2}+5x.$ Which of the following statements are true?

- $f(x)$ is concave down on $(2,\infty )$
- $f(x)$ is concave up on $(2,\infty )$
- $f(x)$ is concave up on $(-\infty ,2)$

choices.value: None of the statements are true

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Intervals of Concavity of a Function
examples.problem: Find the intervals of concavity for the function $f(x) = 2 x^3 - x^4.$
examples.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the second derivative of $f(x),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =2{x}^{3}-{x}^{4} \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =6{x}^{2}-4{x}^{3} \\ {f}^{″}(x) & =12x-12{x}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

To find where the function is concave up, we need to solve $f''(x) > 0\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}12x-12{x}^{2} & >0 \\ 12{x}^{2}-12x & <0 \\ x(x-1) & <0\end{aligned}
$$

We can solve this inequality by considering the graph of $y=x(x-1).$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14043400/assets/54ae61b315630925ec612500a451a90f04b19cf0f5e455c2f3db597c79cebfa1.png)

From the graph, we see that $x(x-1) < 0$ when $0 < x < 1.$   So the graph is concave up on the interval  $(0,1).$

The function $f(x)$ is concave down when $f''(x) <          0.$ By similar reasoning to before, this leads to the inequality $x(x-1)  >        0,$ which has the solution $(-\infty,0)$ and $\left(1,\infty\right).$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14043400/assets/9ac6bf6978169aaa3a29c570234cdbf26f37b6e91488d8e27c63255b8cbb3ba6.png)

The graph above shows $y={f}^{″}(x),$ where the function $f(x)$ is defined on $[0,3].$ Find the intervals on which the function $f(x)$ is concave down.
feedback.worked_solution:
A function $f(x)$ is concave down over an interval $(a,b)$ if ${f}^{″}(x)<0$ for all $x\in (a,b).$

On the given graph of $y={f}^{″}(x),$ we can see that ${f}^{″}(x)<0$ on the interval  $(1,2)$ only. Therefore, the function $f(x)$ is concave down on the interval $(1,2)$ only.
